## Rating

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple" title="Met"}
A README file and a codebook are present. A README file contains at least: 1) a list and descriptions of all files in the replication package; 2) instructions on how to reproduce the results. A codebook should minimally contain: 1) variable labels and descriptions of what those mean; and 2) allowed values of each variable in the dataset.

[Supported by: [#42](../../sources.qmd#p42 "AEA data and code availability policy") README lists all files + purpose/format/provenance + how to replicate; codebook gives allowed values per variable. [#48](../../sources.qmd#p48 "Challenges of curating for reproducible and FAIR research output") codebook: all variables, definitions, values, value labels. [#95](../../sources.qmd#p95 "Computational reproducibility in finance: evidence from 1,000 tests") D3 codebook. [#70](../../sources.qmd#p70 "The Stark realities of reproducible statistically orientated sociological research: Some newer rules of the sociological method") 'no adequate data dictionary -\> fail'. [#55](../../sources.qmd#p55 "Computational reproducibility: a practical framework for data curators")/[#67](../../sources.qmd#p67 "Tools and recommendations for reproducible teaching")/[#137](../../sources.qmd#p137 "Overcoming barriers to computational reproducibility") README explains structure and contents. [#19](../../sources.qmd#p19 "The ReproRubric: evaluation criteria for the reproducibility of computational analyses"), [#57](../../sources.qmd#p57 "Principles for data analysis workflows"), [#69](../../sources.qmd#p69 "The interdependence of data producers and data users: how researchers’ behaviors can support or hinder each other"), [#120](../../sources.qmd#p120 "Reproducibility spectrum for applied social sciences: conceptual taxonomy and recommended tools"), [#97](../../sources.qmd#p97 "Why and how we share reproducible research at yale university’s institution for social and policy studies").]{.source-note}
:::
::: {.callout-warning appearance="simple" title="Partially met"}
Either README or codebook is present, or both are present but their elements required in the "criterion\_met" are incomplete.

[Supported by: [#14](../../sources.qmd#p14 "An empirical analysis of journal policy effectiveness for computational reproducibility") (91% 'data documented', 57% 'software documented'), [#88](../../sources.qmd#p88 "Reproducibility in Management Science") 'insufficient documentation, missing information', [#133](../../sources.qmd#p133 "From guidelines to practice: evaluating the reproducibility of methods in computational social science") 'insufficient detail in README files', [#30](../../sources.qmd#p30 "Advancing computational reproducibility in the dataverse data repository platform") README present but context missing.]{.source-note}
:::
::: {.callout-important appearance="simple" title="Not met"}
Neither README nor codebook are present.

[Supported by: [#17](../../sources.qmd#p17 "Transparency, reproducibility, and the credibility of economics research") 'unlabeled and undocumented mess', [#70](../../sources.qmd#p70 "The Stark realities of reproducible statistically orientated sociological research: Some newer rules of the sociological method") fail without data dictionary, [#58](../../sources.qmd#p58 "Improving research quality: the view from the UK reproducibility network institutional leads for research improvement") data unusable without metadata.]{.source-note}
:::


::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" title="Not applicable"}
Never. When a replication package is a simulation study (C1), evaluate this criteria on the README alone.
:::
